symptoms_text: leaf spots shaped like eyes or spindles with grey centre and brown edge, spots join together and leaves dry up
label: rice_blast
treatment: Spray tricyclazole 75 WP at 0.6 g per litre at the first sign of spots; repeat after 12-15 days if new spots keep appearing. Do not apply extra urea while the disease is active.
prevention: Use blast resistant varieties recommended for your area|Treat seed with tricyclazole or carbendazim 2 g per kg before sowing|Give nitrogen in 3 split doses instead of one heavy dose|Keep the field and bunds free of grassy weeds
source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection: Rice (agritech.tnau.ac.in); Plantwise Knowledge Bank rice blast guide

symptoms_text: round patches of plants suddenly dry up and look burnt, many small brown insects sitting on the stem base just above the water
label: rice_brown_planthopper
treatment: Drain the field for 3-4 days, then spray pymetrozine 50 WG 0.6 g per litre or dinotefuran 20 SG 0.4 g per litre aiming the nozzle at the base of the plants. Do not use synthetic pyrethroids - they make hoppers multiply faster.
prevention: Leave a 30 cm alleyway after every 8-10 rows so air and sunlight reach the base|Give nitrogen in 3 split doses|Avoid needless early sprays so spiders and mirid bugs that eat hoppers survive|Use BPH tolerant varieties where available
source: IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank BPH guide (knowledgebank.irri.org); TNAU Agritech Portal

symptoms_text: yellow orange powder in long stripes along the veins of the leaf, powder sticks to the finger when rubbed, spreading in cold cloudy weather
label: wheat_yellow_rust
treatment: Spray propiconazole 25 EC 1 ml per litre (about 200 ml per acre in 200 litres of water) as soon as the first pustules are seen, covering the whole field, not just patches; repeat after 15 days if it keeps spreading.
prevention: Grow the current rust resistant varieties recommended for your zone|Sow on time|Avoid excess nitrogen|Scout the crop weekly in cool humid weeks of January and February
source: ICAR yellow rust advisory (icar.org.in); ICAR-IIWBR Wheat Crop Health Newsletter (iiwbr.org.in)

symptoms_text: flowers do not open properly and look like a rosette, pink caterpillars inside green bolls, damaged seeds and stained lint
label: cotton_pink_bollworm
treatment: Set 8 pheromone traps per acre; when catches cross about 8 moths per trap for 3 nights, spray profenofos 50 EC 2 ml per litre or emamectin benzoate 5 SG 0.4 g per litre. Pick and destroy rosette flowers and infested bolls every week.
prevention: End the crop by December-January and never keep it as ratoon|Destroy stalks and unopened bolls after the last picking|Use pheromone mating disruption ropes (PBKnot/SPLAT) where your department supplies them|Start trap monitoring from flowering stage
source: ICAR-CICR pink bollworm advisories (cicr.org.in); mating disruption field reports, Down To Earth / Krishak Jagat 2022-23

symptoms_text: large water soaked dark patches on leaves and stems during cool cloudy wet weather, white fungal ring under the leaf, fruits get greasy brown patches, spreads within days
label: tomato_late_blight
treatment: Act fast: remove infected parts and spray cymoxanil 8% + mancozeb 64% WP 3 g per litre; repeat after 10 days. The disease slows down in dry sunny weather.
prevention: Start protective mancozeb 2.5 g per litre sprays when the weather turns cool and cloudy|Avoid overhead evening irrigation|Space plants for air flow|Destroy volunteer potato and tomato plants nearby
source: ICAR-CPRI late blight management studies (cpri.icar.gov.in); TNAU Agritech Portal

symptoms_text: leaves curl upward like a boat, become crinkled and brittle, tiny slender insects run inside leaf folds, flower buds drop and the plant looks bushy and stunted
label: chilli_thrips
treatment: Spray fipronil 5 SC 2 ml per litre or spinosad 45 SC 0.3 ml per litre covering the growing tips; repeat after 15 days if fresh curling continues.
prevention: Do not grow chilli after chilli in the same bed|Hang blue sticky traps for thrips|Light sprinkler irrigation raises humidity and checks thrips|Avoid excess nitrogen
source: ICAR-IIHR and TNAU chilli thrips recommendations (agritech.tnau.ac.in); Indian Journal of Entomology field trials

symptoms_text: ragged holes and window like patches on whorl leaves, wet sawdust like droppings inside the funnel, caterpillar with an inverted Y mark on its head
label: maize_fall_armyworm
treatment: For small larvae drop dry sand or soil mixed with lime into the funnel. If more than 1 in 10 plants show fresh damage, spray emamectin benzoate 5 SG 0.4 g per litre or spinetoram 11.7 SC 0.5 ml per litre directly into the whorl in the evening.
prevention: Set pheromone traps 4 per acre from the first week|Sow on time and together with neighbouring fields|Intercrop maize with pulses|Put up bird perches - birds pick larvae from whorls
source: ICAR fall armyworm advisory; Indian field efficacy trials (Florida Entomologist 2020; Maharashtra/TNAU trials)

symptoms_text: green or brown striped caterpillars first eat leaves then bore round holes in pods and eat the grain with the head inside the pod
label: gram_pod_borer
treatment: While larvae are small spray HaNPV 250 LE 1 ml per litre or neem seed kernel extract 5%. If 1-2 larvae per metre row remain at flowering and podding, spray emamectin benzoate 5 SG 0.4 g per litre.
prevention: Set pheromone traps 4-5 per acre|Fix T shaped bird perches 8-10 per acre - birds pick the caterpillars|Intercrop gram with coriander or linseed|Do not repeat the same insecticide season after season
source: ICAR-IIPR, Kanpur IPM package for chickpea (iipr.icar.gov.in); TNAU Agritech Portal
